summary: Reviewed the full 374-file inventory (api/, FellowScript/, frontend/, desktop/, docs/data) for structure and readability, with a dedicated dead/production-dormant-code pass using git history (this is in fact a git repo) plus codegraph blast-radius/call-path checks to date-stamp staleness rather than just flag non-references. Headline: the legacy vanilla-JS frontend stack (frontend/js/, frontend/css/, account.html/reader.html/signin.html) is confirmed dead in production -- deploy.sh only ships frontend/dist built from frontend/src -- yet was still actively bug-fixed in lockstep with the React app as recently as 5 days before this sweep, with zero CI enforcement (vitest has no test scoping and CI never runs `npm test`) to catch the two stacks diverging. Also found a corrupted absolute-file-path string spliced into Bible mock-data content, unnoticed for ~8 weeks; a stray root-level messages.json diverged-duplicate dead since initial launch (2026-05-14); a stale ios/README_iOS.md describing a project structure that no longer exists; an abandoned convertDict.ipynb superseded by convertDict.py; and confirmed MockDataService.swift is NOT dead (correcting the plan's flagged suspicion) via its UI-TESTING launch-argument wiring. General structure findings: api/db.py (975 lines) mixes live DBManager query code (183 callers) with one-off migration script code with no separation; api/main.py breaks the codebase's own routing convention by keeping all auth/user endpoints inline instead of extracting to api/routes/, including a load_users() naming collision with db.py's differently-scoped function of the same name, and a persist_new_user() docstring describing a dual JSON+Postgres write that no longer happens post-migration.
